statement: When the number $2026$ is written in base $b$, for some integer $b \ge 2$, its last digit is $6$. How many values of $b$ are possible?

choices.misconception: I threw out the divisors 1 and 2 because base 2 has no digit 6, but kept 4 and 5, which have no digit 6 either.
I counted every divisor of 2020 except 1, forgetting that the base must be larger than the digit 6.
I counted all 12 divisors of $2020 = 2^2 \cdot 5 \cdot 101$ without requiring the base to be larger than 6.
I treated the last digit as a remainder of 1 instead of 6 and counted the 14 divisors of 2025 that are larger than 1.

hints: The last digit of a number in base $b$ is its remainder when divided by $b$.
A remainder of 6 means $b$ divides $2026 - 6$, and a remainder is always smaller than the divisor.
$2020 = 2^2 \cdot 5 \cdot 101$ has $3 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 = 12$ divisors. Keep only those greater than 6.

solutions.reliable: The last digit of $2026$ in base $b$ is the remainder of $2026$ on division by $b$. That remainder is $6$ exactly when $b$ divides $2026 - 6 = 2020$ and $b > 6$. Since $2020 = 2^2 \cdot 5 \cdot 101$, its divisors are $1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20, 101, 202, 404, 505, 1010, 2020$. The ones larger than 6 are $10, 20, 101, 202, 404, 505, 1010, 2020$, so there are $8$ bases. Check one: in base $10$ the last digit of $2026$ is indeed $6$. Transferable idea: the last digit in base $b$ is a remainder, so a last-digit condition becomes a divisibility condition plus the rule that a digit is less than the base.
